page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the N1 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, consisting of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 0.9 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud hardware. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield scores of 1125.48 and 2941.66 respectively, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show 25.58 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 21.69 GB/sec for write operations. Software compilation via Clang scored 2740.0, while static web serving throughput reached 2.92 GB/sec.

The n1-highcpu-4 offers a compute-leaning resource allocation with a low memory-to-vCPU ratio. This design presents a trade-off: while it provides dedicated vCPUs, the 4.0 GB memory limit restricts its suitability for memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost perspective, it serves as an entry-level dedicated compute option for workloads that require multi-threading but have minimal memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include lightweight multi-threaded processing, basic software compilation, and low-traffic static web serving.
